newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG SEEK REVENGE AGAINST BORDEAUX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG SEEK REVENGE AGAINST BORDEAUX.

text.p: Paris St Germain will be out for revenge when Bordeaux visit the capital on Saturday, as well as gunning for a morale-boosting victory in their last match before the European Cup Winners' Cup final against Barcelona.
The Parisians were thumped 5-3 the last time they played Bordeaux -- away last November -- and that defeat signalled a slump in fortunes for the French giants.
"We want revenge against them for the 5-3 (defeat) in that away match," PSG's Brazilian coach Ricardo said. "The only way is to pocket three points."

PSG, encouraged by their success so far in their Cup Winners' Cup defence, look to have turned the tide and are determined to hold on to second place in the French league, and with it an automatic place in next season's European Cup.
A 1-0 victory at Lille on Wednesday enabled PSG to string together two league wins in a row for the first time since early November.
"This is a very important match," defender Paul Le Guen said. "It can insure us against any bad surprises in the last two matches. You can count on us to play to our best.
"The (Cup Winners' Cup) final against Barcelona doesn't perturb us at all. After Bordeaux, we'll have 10 days to prepare for it and put our minds to it fully."

Saturday's match will be PSG's fourth in a 10-day spell which began with a nerve-tingling away leg of their Cup Winners' Cup semifinal at Liverpool, where they tooki a battering, lost 2-0 on the night but scraped through 3-2 on aggregate.
"It's beginning to get tough," conceded striker Patrice Loko, who bagged four goals in PSG's 5-0 demolition of Nice last Sunday. "But mentally we feel stronger and stronger."
PSG have a tough run-in to the end of the season with a trip to arch-rivals Marseille and a visit by League Cup holders Strasbourg after the Barcelona clash in Rotterdam on May 14.

The Parisians will be facing an in-form Jean-Pierre Papin on Saturday. The former French international scored twice in Bordeaux's win over PSG in November and has hit three goals in their last three games.

Bordeaux's Ivory Coast defender Cyril Domoraud should be passed fit for the match after having to drop out of Saturday's 2-1 home win over Lens at the last minute when he hurt his hip while warming up.
PSG's recently improved form has sparked interest from foreign clubs for some of the French club's side.

Valencia coach Jorge Valdano, who was at the Parc des Princes on Sunday for the Nice match, has reportedly made an offer for French international goalkeeper Bernard Lama and is said to be also keen to capture central defender Bruno N'Gotty.
Barcelona are highly impressed with PSG's Brazilian captain Rai, the leading force in their recovery this year.
"If you give him time to control the ball and think of how he's going to use it, you're dead," said the Catalan side's spy and former defender Alexanco.
